$comment: The embargoed-report channel, as it actually exists today. BOTH THE MAILBOX AND THE PGP SLOT ARE EMPTY ON PURPOSE. site/build.mjs renders the security page from this file; while `pgp_fingerprint` is empty it prints, in a box, that there is no key and that an unencrypted vulnerability report must not be sent — pointing at a private GitHub security advisory instead, which needs no ceremony and is the path this registry can honestly offer. This is the same shape as the two compiled-in root key slots, which are also empty and which a default build fails closed on. Publishing an address nobody has registered, or a fingerprint for a key nobody holds, teaches a reporter to trust a channel that does not exist — and a vulnerability report sent into a void is worse than one that was never sent, because the reporter believes they told us. Provisioning is a checklist in docs/POLICY.md: register the mailbox, prove it delivers, generate the key offline, publish the fingerprint here and in SECURITY.md in the same commit, then fill in the three fields below.
$comment_advisory: TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE SENTENCE ABOVE, WHICH USED TO CALL A PRIVATE ADVISORY 'END-TO-END TODAY'. (1) A private advisory is PRIVATE, not end-to-end encrypted: it is readable by the reporter, by this repository's admins, and by GitHub. The distinction decides how much detail a reporter pastes into a first message, so it is not a nicety. site/build.mjs still hardcodes the old phrase around `advisory_url` and needs the same correction. (2) `advisory_url` is NOT REACHABLE BY A REPORTER while private vulnerability reporting is off, and it is off — `gh api repos/mihailinl/astra-registry/private-vulnerability-reporting` answered {"enabled":false} on 2026-08-15. GitHub shows the 'Report a vulnerability' form to outside reporters only when that setting is on; with it off the URL works for accounts with write access and 404s for everybody else, which is precisely backwards for a security contact. docs/RUNBOOK.md §1 has the toggle and the check; docs/POLICY.md §11 carries the fallback that works without it (say you have a report, without the details, and the maintainer opens the channel and adds you). Until the toggle is flipped, this field is the maintainer's own link, not a route this registry may advertise to strangers.
email_intended: security@ the domain the catalogue is served from, once that domain is registered and delivery has been proved
